assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles are lipid self-assembly put to work: pH-dependent charge, bilayer and non-bilayer phase behaviour and microfluidic mixing yield particles that encapsulate nucleic acids and release them in the endosome. The physical chemistry of lipid polymorphism translated into a platform that enabled siRNA therapeutics and mRNA vaccines, with very large, concrete impact on medicine.
assessment.attribution: Cullis's group drove the lipid-nanoparticle and ionizable-lipid concept and the rapid-mixing formation process, with Madden and Hope central to the early encapsulation and formulation work. Anderson, Langer and MacLachlan made important later contributions to lipid libraries and siRNA delivery, so the three-person limit forces a hard allocation of credit.
assessment.maturity: Clinically validated at scale since the siRNA drug patisiran and the COVID-19 mRNA vaccines; mechanism and formulation principles are well confirmed by many independent groups. Recognition is timely, though the 2023 Medicine prize for nucleoside-modified mRNA already touched the vaccine application.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees this as chemistry rather than medicine, given the 2023 Medicine prize
Fair split of credit among Cullis, Anderson, Langer and MacLachlan, which the three-name limit cannot fully express
I am working from memory of the history and have not verified who made which formulation advance

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Biomolecular condensates reframe intracellular organization as liquid-liquid phase separation governed by multivalency, weak interactions and thermodynamic phase behaviour. This is a new concept of molecular organization in cells that physical chemists recognize directly, and it reshaped cell biology, disease research (including amyloid-related aggregation) and polymer physics of disordered proteins.
assessment.attribution: Brangwynne and Hyman established P granules as liquids; Rosen and Pappu/Mittag supplied the multivalent-interaction and sequence-grammar framework. Hyman, Brangwynne and Rosen are the most defensible trio, though the theory-side contributors (Pappu, Mittag) are arguably equal in conceptual weight.
assessment.maturity: Rapidly growing and widely reproduced, but there is ongoing debate about the physiological role and the limits of the phase-separation interpretation for specific condensates, so the field is still maturing and parts may be premature.
uncertainties: Controversy over how generally in-vivo condensates are true phase-separated liquids and what is functional
Credit split between experimental biology and the physical-chemical theory contributors
Fit with the Chemistry versus Physiology or Medicine remit

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Metal-directed self-assembly of discrete cages and capsules shows how thermodynamically controlled, reversible coordination yields well-defined supramolecular architectures in high yield. It is a clear conceptual advance in molecular organization, with host-guest chemistry, confined catalysis and stabilization of reactive species as applications.
assessment.attribution: Fujita's coordination cages, Raymond's tetrahedral M4L6 hosts and Stang's molecular-panelling and directional-bonding approach are the principal independent founding lines; Nitschke and Ward are important later developers. A Fujita-Raymond-Stang trio is plausible, but Sauvage, Stoddart and Cram-type prizes already honoured parts of supramolecular chemistry.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with decades of independent confirmation and broad adoption; recognition is overdue rather than premature, though application impact outside chemistry is modest compared with the leading candidates.
uncertainties: Overlap with earlier supramolecular Nobel prizes could count against it
Priority and credit between the independent Fujita, Raymond and Stang lines
Practical impact beyond fundamental host-guest chemistry

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation turns the cell's ubiquitin-proteasome machinery against chosen proteins by induced proximity, via heterobifunctional PROTACs and molecular glues. It opens drug targets previously considered undruggable and is a new chemical concept, with multiple compounds in clinical trials.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies conceived and first demonstrated PROTACs; Ciulli made the first VHL-based small-molecule PROTACs and structural work. The thalidomide-cereblon glue mechanism (Handa, Ito) is a separate and important line, so the compound discovery may need different recognition and the trio cannot cover it.
assessment.maturity: Strong early validation and clinical-stage compounds, but clinical efficacy and approvals are still emerging, which makes the timing slightly early.
uncertainties: Clinical outcomes remain incomplete, so the long-term impact is not yet settled
Allocation between PROTACs and the molecular-glue/cereblon story
I am working from memory of the credit history and have not verified details

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Energy landscape theory with the funnel concept explains how proteins fold quickly and reliably, reducing Levinthal's paradox to statistical mechanics of rugged landscapes with minimal frustration. It is a unifying physical-chemical principle that also links to misfolding and aggregation, close to my own thinking on thermodynamics and phase behaviour.
assessment.attribution: Wolynes and Onuchic, with Bryngelson, developed the funnel and principle of minimal frustration; Dill contributed hydrophobic-collapse and lattice-model foundations; Fersht's experimental phi-value analysis provided the key empirical test. Deciding between theory and experiment is the main attribution difficulty.
assessment.maturity: Conceptually well established over three decades and widely used, now largely overtaken in practice by AI structure prediction (2024 Chemistry prize), which may reduce urgency or prompt a view of it as already adjacent.
uncertainties: The 2024 prize for protein structure prediction and design may make the committee reluctant to return to protein folding
Theory versus experiment credit (Fersht) and Bryngelson's role
Mostly conceptual impact with less direct technological application

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Surfactant-templated ordered mesoporous silicas use liquid-crystalline self-assembly of amphiphiles to build materials with tunable pores of 2-50 nm. It is a striking example of soft-matter self-assembly transferred to inorganic materials chemistry, with uses in catalysis, adsorption and separation.
assessment.attribution: The Mobil group (Kresge, Beck and colleagues) reported M41S/MCM-41, and Inagaki independently reported FSM-16; Stucky, Zhao and Ryoo extended the field with SBA-15 and related materials. Credit within the Mobil team is distributed and the independent Japanese work complicates a trio.
assessment.maturity: Mature and extensively confirmed, with broad adoption, but commercial impact has been narrower than for zeolites, and the discovery dates to the early 1990s so the moment may be past.
uncertainties: Industrial impact is less than the scientific concept might suggest
Distributed credit among Mobil team members and the independent Inagaki work
Memory-based recollection of the Mobil author roles; not verified

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Self-assembled monolayers, especially thiols on gold, and soft lithography give molecular-level control of interfacial structure and wetting and enabled microcontact printing and microfluidics. This is classic surface and colloid chemistry with a lasting influence on both materials science and biointerface research.
assessment.attribution: Nuzzo and Allara reported alkanethiolate monolayers on gold, Sagiv the earlier silane monolayers, and Whitesides developed the broad SAM and soft-lithography programmes. Priority among Sagiv, Nuzzo/Allara and Whitesides is a real attribution tension.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature with very wide independent use; if anything recognition is late, and the field's frontier has moved on.
uncertainties: Priority disputes between early silane and thiol monolayer work
Whitesides's breadth of contributions may be hard to confine to a single discovery
Perceived as a tool and method more than a single decisive discovery

assessment.nobel_worthiness: DNA origami and programmable DNA nanostructures show that Watson-Crick base pairing can specify arbitrary two- and three-dimensional objects through thermodynamically and kinetically controlled self-assembly. It is a major concept in molecular organization with applications in nanofabrication, sensing and molecular machines.
assessment.attribution: Rothemund introduced scaffolded DNA origami; Winfree and Rothemund's algorithmic self-assembly, Yan's 2D and 3D DNA nanostructures and Shih's and Yin's 3D origami and tile systems were all decisive. Seeman's founding role in DNA nanotechnology is not among the supplied names, which complicates a fair prize configuration.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed as a method, but practical applications remain limited, and the field is still exploring where it leads; recognition could be seen as somewhat early.
uncertainties: Seeman is not among the credited names, so a fair attribution may be impossible with this list
Limited real-world application so far
